report:
Initial stage (P00–P07 and the supplied P15–P42 selections): packaging attracted praise for appearance, refillability and perceived environmental merits, alongside one detailed arrival-leak complaint. Updated stage adds P08–P13 and R01: arrival leakage becomes a repeated, thread-concentrated customer report, while a separate Softwear review documents leakage during pocket carriage. Reception is mixed: praise, failures and loyalty coexist. The initial-stage boundary follows the supplied initial/added ordering; no separate initial-stage record was supplied.

Initial reception: P00’s metal-packaging praise drew 296 displayed likes; the brand’s agreement P01 drew 39. P03 is the same actor as P00, offering qualified recycling/reuse speculation, not independent verification. P02 questions recyclability. Environmental benefit therefore remains unverified. Distinct accounts repeat favorable packaging judgments (P21, P26, P38–P40), but generally with one like each; P26 also asks what the product does for skin. P15’s intended empty-container reuse drew 150 likes, supporting resonance with that proposal, not completed reuse. P42 reports receiving a product and only then discovering its refillability. The comment bodies do not establish the pictured or complained-about SKU/version; the supplied product catalog cannot resolve this.

Initial failure/remedy: P06 reports arrival leakage with a loose top, opening and cleaning the package, and concern about oxygen exposure (12 likes). This is one detailed customer account, not a verified defect mechanism or evidence of spoiled product. P07, the brand (12 likes), says short exposure is not an issue and offers a replacement conditional on contact. This establishes the offer and brand reassurance, not replacement dispatch or independently established product safety.

Updated failure support: seven focal TikTok accounts report or contextually agree to arrival leakage: P06, P08–P13. Two explicitly describe a loose/improperly screwed top (P06, P13); P08 adds Sephora ordering and a free replacement reportedly sent. Four are bare agreements (P09–P12), which support the parent’s arrival-leak proposition in context without independently supplying its loose-top, cleanup or oxygen details. These are seven distinct visible account identities in one reply branch, not seven verified independent humans or events. Displayed likes respectively are 12, 5, 4, 4, 2, 0 and 0. P13’s detailed major-leak report remains material despite zero likes. Repeated arrival leakage is supported at the distinct-account level within this thread; exposure, prevalence, root cause, affected SKU/version and independence beyond account identity remain unknown.

R01 separately reports Softwear–Void’s lid repeatedly unscrewing and a leak in a work pocket, with clothing stains, lost product and inability to return recovered product to the package. This is not another arrival-leak report or evidence about the unidentified TikTok package. The accounts repeat the broader experience of packaging leakage across TikTok and a retailer review, but product and use-condition differences prevent exact cross-venue corroboration of an arrival defect or a shared mechanism. R01 proposes a click-lock closure or doe-foot option; neither is a delivered remedy. Its 3-star rating, recommendation=true, verified-buyer=true and rewarded=false are native metadata; helpful-vote/like engagement is unavailable. Product-wide rating aggregates are not engagement with this review.

Buying and loyalty: P17 reports an all-Experiment routine and Continuum in the mail; P20 expresses buying enthusiasm without confirming completed checkout; P32 tentatively anticipates saving up; P38 intends to try. P04 and P27 request refill bundles, the latter naming Continuum and Super Saturated; neither establishes purchase or repurchase. P29 asks about a sticker in a refill. None establishes packaging as a completed-purchase driver. P08 reports a free replacement sent, not delivered, and identifies Sephora as the apparent service provider. R01 explicitly intends to repurchase despite packaging dissatisfaction because Void is a favorite, while also recommending it. That is complaint alongside loyalty, not completed repurchase. No explicit abandonment, return or packaging-driven switching is reported.

Initial requested-count values were arrival_leak=1, explicit_loose_top=1, bare_arrival_agreement=0, replacement_offered=1, replacement_sent=0, retailer_leak=0, repurchase_intended=0. The counts array gives updated values and exact focal sets. Counts are source-account counts under the requested definitions, not origin or event counts.

Provenance and limits: all P records are comments on https://www.tiktok.com/@experimentwrld/video/7639858768146222366, observed 2026-09-09T11:56:25.935Z. Dates below are displayed month-day with year unavailable; engagement is displayed likes at that observation. P01/P07 are the same brand actor; P00/P03 are the same commenter. No context-only records were supplied. Capture exposes 47 comment bodies against 72 advertised comments; only the arrival-leak and metal-packaging reply branches were expanded. Native comment IDs are unavailable. Likes show endorsement, not verified experiences, independent origins, prevalence or buying effects; small values lack sufficient exposure context for material-resonance claims. No directly opposing leak testimony is present in this bounded set, but favorable packaging reception does not refute leaks, and neither establishes overall reliability.
